parsed.why: Strong state layer: gender-identity nondiscrimination since 2001, hate-crime enhancements, panic defence repealed, X markers, shield law. But national border/passport and airport screening exposures are unchanged and no enforcement or violence data exists.

Best local layer: public-accommodation and employment protections, strengthened hate-crime law, 2022 shield law, and custody/strip-search placement by recognised gender — the harshest local tier-1 exposure removed. National border and screening rules still govern.

Robust public-accommodation, hate-crime reporting machinery, shield law, confidential name change, X markers. Unrepealed (unenforced) sodomy provisions touch a trans visitor's relationship only nominally; national entry and screening exposure unchanged.

Below parent: school facility restriction by birth sex, minor care ban, surgery-gated birth certificates, hate-crime statute excluding gender identity, religious-exemption statute, protections only municipal in 19 cities. Recourse for a targeted visitor is thin.

Statewide gender-identity protections across public accommodation and services, hate-crime enhancements, panic defence abolished, X markers since 2017, 2023 shield law (scope narrowed). Religious-employer exemption and unchanged national border rules hold it below the top.
